experiment: seed-level comparison of the three lunar detectors (A3)
why: Every earlier comparison rested on ONE seed per model plus a paired bootstrap over 19 test files, which resamples files but not training stochasticity. Injection training draws fresh synthetic events every epoch, so the seed is a first-order source of variance and must be in the error bar. Five seeds is the standard bar.
protocol: Each seed trained with identical hyperparameters and evaluated at its OWN val-tuned operating point (eval_unet.py); test never touched during selection.

seiscnn_vs_specunet_screened.conclusion: The supervised detector is significantly better at the seed level. The earlier 'statistically indistinguishable' claim does NOT survive proper seed accounting - it came from a single-seed paired bootstrap that resampled test files but held the trained model fixed.

noise_screen_effect.conclusion: Screening the ~8.4% Nakamura-contaminated noise windows has NO measurable effect on benchmark F1. The single-seed 0.440 -> 0.407 drop reported before this experiment was seed noise, not an effect.

headline_checkpoint_caveat: The frozen v1.0 SpecUNet number, F1 0.440, is the MAXIMUM of its three seeds; the seed mean is 0.379. Any single-checkpoint figure in this repository should be read alongside the seed distribution, not as a typical draw.
revised_claim: Injection-only training, using ZERO labelled positive windows, reaches 74.7% of the supervised detector's mean F1 (0.372 vs 0.498). That is the defensible statement. It is not parity, and it should not be described as such.
what_this_does_not_fix: Seed variance is now properly accounted, but the evaluation set is still 19 continuous test files / 19 events. No amount of reseeding addresses that; only a larger labelled evaluation set would.
